about.description: Plain-language guide to every column in this image complexity dataset. Each image has been measured in many ways to estimate how 'hard' it is to work with — both for a person drawing the outlines and for a computer trying to recognize the objects in it.
about.how_to_read_values: Most measurements are scores between 0 and 1, where 0 means 'not at all' and 1 means 'completely' or 'as much as possible'. A few are plain counts or real-world units (like pixels or meters), and a handful are just labels or file paths. The 'scale' field tells you which is which.

groups.Basic info: Where the image lives and its basic size.
groups.How hard to outline: Measures of how tricky the object edges and shapes are to trace.
groups.How crowded: Measures of how many objects there are and how much they overlap.
groups.Object types: Measures about the different kinds of objects in the image.
groups.Photo quality: Measures of blur, brightness, and lighting problems.
groups.Object colors: Measures based on the colors of the objects.
groups.Background: Measures of how busy or distracting the background and surroundings are.
groups.Object shapes: Measures of how irregular the object shapes are.
groups.Annotation coverage: Checks of how completely the objects were outlined.
groups.Camera & sensor info: Facts about the camera and how the photo was taken (from the camera's own records).
groups.Final scores: The overall difficulty rating and grouping.

image_path.plain_meaning: The location of the photo file on the computer.

width.plain_meaning: How wide the photo is, measured in pixels (dots).

height.plain_meaning: How tall the photo is, measured in pixels (dots).

instance_count.plain_meaning: The raw number of separate object shapes found — including tiny specks that may be mistakes in the outline.

real_instance_count.plain_meaning: The number of real object shapes after throwing out the tiny specks that are likely outlining mistakes. This is the trustworthy count.

mean_instance_area_ratio.plain_meaning: The average size of an object in the photo, compared to the whole image. Small values mean lots of little objects.

instance_area_std.plain_meaning: How much the object sizes differ from each other. High values mean the photo mixes big and small objects together.

overlap_ratio.plain_meaning: How much the objects touch or pile on top of each other. High values mean a tangled, crowded scene where objects merge together — one of the hardest things to separate.

class_count.plain_meaning: How many different kinds of things (object types, categories, etc.) are labeled in the photo.

smallest_class_ratio.plain_meaning: How balanced the object types are. Low values mean one type barely shows up compared to the others — rare types are easy to miss.

class_entropy.plain_meaning: How evenly the different object types are mixed. High values mean a rich, varied mix of types; low means one type dominates.

blur_laplacian.plain_meaning: How sharp and in-focus the photo is. High values mean a crisp photo; low values mean it's blurry or out of focus.

overexpose_ratio.plain_meaning: How much of the photo is too bright and washed out, like a blown-out white sky. Bright spots hide object detail.

underexpose_ratio.plain_meaning: How much of the photo is too dark, like deep shadows where you can't see detail. Dark spots can hide and merge objects together.

shadow_edge_ratio.plain_meaning: How many shadow lines cut across the photo. Shadow edges can look like fake object edges and cause confusion.

mean_pairwise_color_dist.plain_meaning: How much the colors vary within a single labeled object. When objects are tangled together, one outline accidentally grabs colors from several objects, so this goes up. It's one of the best signs of a tangled, hard image.

interclass_color_sim.plain_meaning: How similar different object types look in color. High values mean two categories look almost the same — easy to mix up. (Only meaningful when there's more than one type.)

green_mass.plain_meaning: A measure of how much of a specific reference color (green) appears in the photo overall — a general color-based proxy for how much of the labeled foreground is present.
green_mass.scale: Number (higher = more of that color present)

annotated_px_count.plain_meaning: How many dots (pixels) were marked as an object in the outline.

green_annotation_ratio.plain_meaning: Whether the green-colored regions in the photo were fully outlined. Values near 1 mean the outlining covered those areas well; low values mean there are green regions that nobody outlined — a sign of a possible mistake.

wb_r_gain.plain_meaning: How much the camera boosted the red tones to balance the colors. A technical color-correction setting.

wb_b_gain.plain_meaning: How much the camera boosted the blue tones to balance the colors. A technical color-correction setting.

wb_rb_ratio.plain_meaning: The balance between red and blue color correction. It hints at the warmth or coolness of the lighting and whether colors drifted between photos.

complexity_score.plain_meaning: The overall difficulty rating for the image, combining all the measurements above into one number. Values near 1 mean the image is hard in many ways at once — for both people and computers. This is the main number used to rank images from easy to hard.

category.plain_meaning: Which kind of difficulty best describes this image, as a group number from 1 to 10. For example, one group is for tangled, crowded scenes, another for poor lighting, and so on. Group 10 is special: it means the image is hard in several different ways at the same time.
